confirmed.title: Skipped outbox entries are never deleted and fill the only page the script reads, so other residents' app cases stop reaching the sheet without any error
confirmed.scenario:
1. A programme resident is on the app's residents list (People, e.g. a new intake or an id typo) but not on the response sheet's Residents tab, or their rid is not 6 digits.
2. They log cases in the app. Each one creates sheetOutbox/{caseId}, which the rules allow because the rid matches their logbook.
3. Every 5 minutes logbookOutboxRun lists the outbox with '?pageSize=12'. There is no pageToken and no orderBy, so it always gets the first 12 documents by id. logbookOutboxAdd_ skips this resident's entries (lines 135-136), and they are never deleted.
4. Once about a dozen of these stuck entries have low ids, the first page is mostly or entirely stuck entries. Other residents' new entries whose random uid() ids sort after them are never listed.
5. The run logs only console.warn for skipped entries (lines 307-308). s.errors stays empty, so the execution shows 'Completed' and no failure email goes out.
confirmed.consequence: The sheet silently stops getting most residents' new app cases. The Case tab, Database, resident reports and AY totals fall further behind the app every hour, until someone notices (the weekly drift check) and fixes the Residents tab. The nightly Totals check cannot see it because it only compares the sheet with itself. In the simulation, the other residents' cases still not in the sheet grew from 2 of 29 at 12 h to 187 of 276 at 72 h, and every run 'succeeded'.
confirmed.fix: Read past the stuck entries. Either list with pageToken until BATCH processable entries are found, or list a larger page (e.g. pageSize=300) and drop entries whose rid isn't on the Residents sheet before taking the first 12. Add orderBy=createdAt so the oldest go first. Make a skip loud: push skipped entries into s.errors, or throw once a day while any are waiting, so the trigger owner gets the failure email. Add a test with more than 12 unprocessable entries plus one good entry whose id sorts last.
verifier_fix:
The proposed direction is right; one caution and one simplification:
1. Never add orderBy=createdAt while still reading a single page. The stuck entries are the oldest, so they would then fill page 1 every time and stop everything once 12 are stuck. Only add the ordering together with reading past skipped entries.
2. Simplest version: in logbookOutboxRun, list with a larger page (e.g. pageSize=300, following nextPageToken up to a cap) ordered by createdAt. Build io, drop entries that are not 6 digits or not io.residentOk(rid) into a skipped list, and pass only the first LOGBOOK_OUTBOX_BATCH processable entries to the cycle.
3. Make skips loud without blocking the other residents: after the cycle, throw (so the trigger owner gets the failure email) if any skipped entry is older than about 24 h. Optionally keep a Script property so this fires at most once a day.
4. Add a test with 13 or more unprocessable entries whose ids sort first, plus one good entry whose id sorts last, and assert that the good entry is added.

confirmed.title: Deleting a case then tapping Undo (or restoring it from the recycle bin) within the pick-up window means it never reaches the sheet
confirmed.scenario:
1. A programme resident logs a case. createCase calls toSheet and sheetOutbox/{id} is created.
2. Within about 5 minutes, before Outbox.gs picks it up, they delete it (edit dialog Delete, list multi-delete, or the Case tab's Undo when typing has started). moveToBin calls removeCase, and removeCase calls offSheet([id]), which deletes the outbox entry.
3. They tap Undo on 'Case moved to the recycle bin' (bin.js:91), or later use Settings > Recycle bin > Restore. restoreFromBin calls restoreCase (bin.js:150), which saves the case again but never calls toSheet.
4. The same happens when the write queue undoes the delete: a delete that conflicts with an edit on another device, so the case is kept (bin.js:110), or a failed delete restored by rollBack (bin.js:112). The entry was already dropped because writes.save resolves after 180 ms, before the server answers.
confirmed.consequence: The case is in the app (and counts there) but is never added to the response sheet's Case tab, Database, resident report or AY totals. The app and sheet counts differ by one per case, permanently (no back-fill).
confirmed.fix: Queue the entry again when a deleted case comes back. Export toSheet (or a requeueSheet(c) helper) from ui-core.js and call it after restoreCase in restoreFromBin's case branch and in rollBack's case branches, including the conflict branch, where the kept case needs its entry back. This is safe even if the row is already in the sheet: Outbox.gs finds 'app:<id>' in column J and just deletes the entry, and the rules allow the create because the earlier delete removed the document. If cases created before 14 Oct should not be back-filled, only re-queue when createdAt is on or after the switch-on time. Add 'delete, Undo, entry back' to the sheetOutbox e2e scenario.
verifier_fix:
Mostly right; four refinements.
(1) Do not put toSheet inside restoreCase itself. The edit Undo ("Case updated", ui-log.js:1341) also calls restoreCase, and it would then re-queue every edited case. Add an exported `requeueSheet(c)` in ui-core.js (a toSheet wrapper) and call it explicitly where a deleted case comes back.
(2) In restoreFromBin, re-queue only when the id is unchanged (`out.id === e.data.id`). If a new uid was assigned because a live copy exists, the original may already be in the sheet as `app:<oldId>`, and queuing the new id would add a duplicate row.
(3) In rollBack's conflict branch (bin.js:110), the case kept is the newer remote version, not `e.data`. Queue `S.cases.find(x => x.id === e.data.id) || job.remote || e.data`. In the restore branch (bin.js:112), queue after restoreCase.
(4) Keep the createdAt >= switch-on (14 Oct 2026) guard. toSheet already applies the source filter (app/paste only) through outboxEntry.

Alternative for the write-queue paths: drop the outbox entry in moveToBin's watchDeletes only once `writes.status` is 'synced', not inside removeCase. Then a delete that conflicts or fails never removes the entry, and only an explicit Undo or Restore needs a re-queue. The direct removeCase caller at ui-log.js:1026 would keep its own immediate offSheet.
Add 'delete, Undo, entry back' and 'bin Restore, entry back' to the conflicts.emulator sheetOutbox scenario.

confirmed.title: The column J duplicate check uses markers read before the lock, and nothing stops two runs at once, so overlapping runs add every case twice
confirmed.scenario:
1. Two logbookOutboxRun executions start close together. This happens if a second sheet editor runs logbookOutboxSetup: ScriptApp.getProjectTriggers() lists only the caller's own triggers, so `has` is false and a second 5-minute trigger is added, even though the README says 'Safe to run again' and says to recreate the trigger from another editor. It also happens if someone presses Run on logbookOutboxRun in the editor during a trigger run.
2. Each run lists the outbox and reads column J's app: markers once, in logbookOutboxIo_ (lines 253-260), without holding any lock.
3. Run A gets the document lock first, appends rows, writes app:<id>, and deletes the entries.
4. Run B gets the lock next. Its io.markers is the snapshot taken before A's appends, so line 131 `if (io.markers[mark])` misses them and B appends the same cases again, plus Database rows and rebuilds.
confirmed.consequence: Duplicate Case-tab rows, each with app:<id>, and duplicate Database rows, so resident reports and AY totals count each case twice. The sheet then disagrees with the app. The nightly Totals check cannot repair it, because it compares the Database against a Case tab that itself holds the duplicate row. The README's 'A case is never added twice' promise does not hold under concurrency.
confirmed.fix: At the top of logbookOutboxRun, take a script-wide lock: `var run = LockService.getScriptLock(); if (!run.tryLock(0)) return;` and release it in finally. This stops two runs whichever user's trigger started them. Also check the marker inside each locked chunk before appending: re-read column J, or use a TextFinder for 'app:'+id on column J. Say in the README that setup must be run by one person only.
verifier_fix:
The proposed fix is right; three refinements:
(1) In logbookOutboxRun, take `var run = LockService.getScriptLock(); if (!run.tryLock(0)) { console.log('Another outbox run is going; skipped.'); return; }` before getPending/list, and release it in a finally around the whole run, rebuilds included. The script lock covers every user and every execution of the project, so it also stops a second user's trigger and a press of Run. It also fixes the LOGBOOK_OUTBOX_PENDING read-modify-write race.
(2) As defence in depth, inside each env.locked hold, check `caseSheet.getRange(2, 10, last-1, 1).createTextFinder('app:'+id).matchEntireCell(true).findNext()` (or re-read column J) before appending. Call SpreadsheetApp.flush() before releasing the document lock, so the next holder sees the appended rows.
(3) In logbookOutboxSetup, getProjectTriggers can't see other users' triggers. Record the trigger owner in a Script property (Session.getEffectiveUser().getEmail()) and refuse, or warn, if a different account runs setup. Change the README's "Safe to run again" to "safe for the same account; only one person sets it up".

confirmed.title: A resident added to the programme list after already using the app gets no outbox entries for that whole session, because S.logbook.rid is never set locally
confirmed.scenario:
1. Someone signs in to the app before an admin puts them on the residents list. That has happened: two such accounts on 12 Oct, per PLAN-app-to-sheet.md. readWho() caches {resident: null} on the device.
2. The admin adds them in People.
3. They next open the app. onUser uses the cached `known` (resident null), so the rid-save at app.js:1016 is skipped. refreshWho then sets S.resident from the server, but the server logbook has no rid. S.logbook (app.js:942) either stays as it was or is replaced by a copy without rid.
4. Every case logged in that session reaches toSheet (ui-core.js:454) with `S.logbook?.rid === S.resident.rid` false (undefined vs '2026xx'), so nothing is queued, silently.
5. Only on a later start does app.js:1016 save the rid. Even then cloud.saveLogbook doesn't update S.logbook, which gets the rid only if refreshWho replaces it.
confirmed.consequence: Real cases of a listed programme resident never reach the response sheet. There is no back-fill, so app and sheet counts stay different for those cases. In an installed phone app, one 'session' can last days.
confirmed.fix: Wherever the rid is saved, also set it locally: `S.logbook = { ...S.logbook, rid: resident.rid }` after saveLogbook at app.js:1016. In refreshWho, when w.resident is set and S.logbook.rid !== w.resident.rid, call cloud.saveLogbook({ rid }) and set S.logbook.rid too. The sheetOutbox create rule checks logbooks/{me}.rid, and Firestore sends the logbook write before the outbox write, so the create will pass.
verifier_fix:
At app.js:1016, set the rid in place so the identity check in refreshWho still works: `if (resident && logbook.rid !== resident.rid) { logbook.rid = resident.rid; cloud.saveLogbook(user.email, { rid: resident.rid }).catch(() => {}); }`. Here `logbook === S.logbook`, so this also updates S.logbook. Do not replace the object.

In refreshWho, after the lb replacement and adoptShared lines (so a server copy without rid can't overwrite it), add: `const r = S.resident; if (r && r.rid && S.logbook && S.logbook.rid !== r.rid) { S.logbook.rid = r.rid; cloud.saveLogbook(user.email, { rid: r.rid }).catch(() => {}); }`. Optionally add an emulator test: sign in unlisted, add the resident, reload with the cached who, log a case, and expect a sheetOutbox entry.
